differences.what: roof: the engraving's mansard, its steep lower faces bowed a little to a curb about 2.9 m over the cornice, under a low upper hip; the build's was a 30-degree tin hip

wall head: the engraving's cornice stands 10.9 m over grade (its soffit 10.61 m at both front corners, y 300 and 327 px) on T-2437's re-solved camera, 8.9 m over the 2.0 m principal floor; the build's walls stood at 8.2 m on a 1.4 m floor (T-2370 read the same pixels as 8.2 m on an eye 0.7 m under grade). Built so by T-2437: storeys 4.8 and 4.1 m on the 2.0 m floor, the cornice landing on the drawn one

north pavilion: the north 3.75 m of the front (v 7.5-11.25) is a pavilion standing a little proud, with two round-headed windows a storey under moulded hoods and a light corner strip at its north corner; the build's front is flat there and carries the canted bay
crown: over the pavilion a taller bell-curved mansard with one round-headed dormer, rising about 0.7 m over the main curb; the build has none

corner strip: the engraving draws a light strip down the pavilion's north corner, a stone or painted quoin, from x 686-688 px to the corner (695-700 px); T-2404's pavilion turned that corner in its own brick. Built so by T-2462: a K08 strip of dressed stone 0.4 m wide and 0.04 m proud on the pavilion's front at its north corner, from its plinth to its wall head, landing at x 682-697 px (its stone is RECONSTRUCTED: the print cannot tell stone from paint)

dormers: round-headed dormers in the mansard's lower face, two seen on the north face, their arch heads at x 746 and 805 px (51 and 110 px behind the crown's front-north corner) reaching about 10.5 m, just under the curb; built so by T-2411, two K06 round-arched sash in stone faces at u 12.6 and 6.1 m, landing at x 756 and 813 px, 47 and 106 px behind the build's crown corner (which itself stands about 10 px right of the engraving's). The engraver draws both wider and more frontal than the camera allows; the front's lower slope is behind the trees

bay window: a one-storey canted bay on the SOUTH part of the front, its front's edges at x 437 and 488 px and its north cheek's foot at 512 px (v 1.54-4.64, 0.58 m out), two round-headed lights in its front, under a flared hood on a console at each corner of its front with a row of modillions; built so by T-2408 (k08.bay.canted_hooded), its edges landing at x 440 and 492 px. The picture's finial is the foot of the upper window that stands on the hood's top, and is not a finial

windows: round-headed sash under moulded hoods on the street front, the upper window over the bay and the one over the door each with an ornate crown over its hood; the north wall's windows flat-headed, two a storey, at x 737 and 810 px (3.35 and 11.55 m back from the front corner). Built so by T-2410: both upper street windows K06's round-headed fanlight sash in a round hole through the brick under the kit's stone arch band, a key block on each crown for the ornament the engraving draws but does not resolve; the north wall's three windows a storey are now the engraving's two, flat-headed

the upper window over the door: the engraving draws it south of the door's centre, its frames at x 518-552 px; the build stood it on the door's v 6.6 (K01 put a storey's windows on the bays below). Built so by T-2462: K01 takes an upper storey's own window centres (front_bays_by_storey) and the window stands at v 5.5, landing at x 522-550 px. The window over the bay window likewise: drawn with its jambs at x 441-470 px where the build stood it on the bay's v 3.09 (x 459-484), now at v 2.5, landing at x 445-470

entrance: the door beside the pavilion's south face under a hood, reached by a straight stoop whose north string is the rail rising to the right from x 540 to 582 px (on this camera a line running back toward the wall draws so; one running north along the front would rise over about 80 px, not 42), at its head a porch at the principal floor running north before the pavilion to the north corner behind a turned balustrade that carries on down the stoop. Built (T-2409): the door at v 6.6 under a K09 cornice hood on consoles, the straight stoop's north string at v 7.65 (drawn at x 572 to 541 px), a stone terrace 1.2 m deep before the pavilion to the corner (its north end at x 685.6 px against the engraving's 690) behind a turned balustrade carried down both cheeks. The engraving drew this front's floor, porch and fence about 1.5-2 m lower against the house than the old camera's grade put them; that was the camera's height datum (T-2406), re-solved by T-2437 from the street fence's foot on the walk: the porch's rail top now reads 2.91-2.93 m, the principal floor 2.0 m, and the build's floor, porch, stoop and balustrade, raised to it, land on the drawn ones

the door: with the window over it moved (T-2462), the engraving draws the door under it, its panelled leaves at x 532-562 px (v about 5.4-6.45) under a hood at x 505-552 px, where the build stands it on v 6.6 (x 548-581 px). The stoop is where both pictures put it (the engraving's north string running back to v 7.65, the Tribune sketch's stoop straight from the gate at v 6.3-7.5 at the street line), so the door stands at the south end of a landing that runs on north into the porch; K07 centres its stoop on its door and has to learn one off the door's axis (T-2463)

fence: a lattice of interlaced pointed arches on a solid base along the street line, and from about x 670 px (v 12.6 on the street line) a close-boarded fence that turns at the north lot line and runs back along it; built so by T-2414 (k11.fence.lattice_arcade, arches three bays of 0.3 m wide, on the kit's curb, then k11.fence.side_boards 1.5 m high), the boards taking over at x 668 px. On T-2437's camera the lattice's foot (y 648-650 px) is the eye's height control and its top (y 596 px) reads 1.50 m; the build's lattice top lands within about 6 px of it

chimney: a tall stack at the front of the north wall, rising from the cornice beside the crown, its lit east face at x 703-722 px and its north face to 730 px; built so by T-2414, a 0.75 by 0.6 m stack standing on the cornice astride the north wall line (centre u 15.935, v 11.5), projecting to 703.5, 721.6 and 730.0 px, its cap at 12.5 m (y 175 px); the build's second ridge stack over the front half, where the engraving draws sky over the crown, is gone. On T-2437's re-solved camera every height rises 2.7 m and the cap went up with the walls to 15.2 m; see 'crown and front stack' for what that leaves

crown and front stack: re-read on the overlay of T-2437's render, the crown's top stood at y 171-175 px between x 640 and 680 where the engraving draws it at 189-190 px, about 0.5 m high, and the front stack's cap at y 154-157 px against the drawn 174-176 (14.55-14.65 m over grade). Built so by T-2444: the crown's curb 0.3 m over the main curb, the least K01 allows, its top now at y 183-190 px between x 620 and 680; the stack at K01's least 0.6 m over it, its cap at 14.7 m, y 169-170 px; and the crown's dormer, which the engraving draws low on the crown's face (its surround y 212-267 px) and the build had about 0.7 m higher, now at about y 210-263 px, its face 0.027 m in from the crown's fascia on a 0.1 m sill

roof covering: the lower faces and the crown's read as slate in courses; built so by T-2414 (K04 Pennsylvania slate on every face steeper than 45 degrees, the low upper hip, which the picture cannot see, staying tin)

bay window's heights: on T-2437's re-solved camera the engraving draws the bay's lights from 3.09 m (y 545 px, 1.1 m over the 2.0 m floor) to their arch tops at 5.71 m (y 466 px), the hood's eaves at 6.24 m (y 450 px), level with the pavilion's principal-storey heads (6.23-6.37 m), and the hood's top at 7.46 m (y 413 px), under the upper window's foot (7.54 m). Built so by T-2444: the bay's storey 5.93 m to its wall top, its lights 3.09-5.67 m, its eaves' fascia top at 6.18 m and the hood meeting the wall at 7.34 m, 0.15 m under the upper sash's sill as K01 requires; on the overlay the hood's eaves, the lights' arches and the hood's top land on the drawn ones

bay window's tone: the engraving draws the bay dark against the light front, its cheeks hatched as boards and its hood's slate in courses (the hood's shadow, or a painted timber bay). Built by T-2444 as painted timber (K08's frame fabric, the sash's dark green paint on boards over a brick plinth), so it reads dark against the front as drawn; timber rather than shaded brick is RECONSTRUCTED, which the monochrome print cannot decide

bay window's terrace: a low turned balustrade runs before the bay at its foot, from x 365 to 460 px, its rail's top at y 551 px, 2.89 m over grade on T-2437's camera: the principal floor's level, so it reads as the porch's terrace carried south across the bay's front and on past the south corner. Built so by T-2450: the stoop's terrace to its LEFT (K07's terrace mirrored), from the landing's south edge (v 5.7) to v -0.35, 1.2 m deep, its back stepped out to the bay's front, behind the north terrace's turned balustrade; on the overlay its rail's top lands at y 551 px and its south newel's face at x 364 px, against the drawn 551 and 364-365. Where it joins the landing (x 460-540 px) the engraving draws the tree and a shrub before it, so that it joins is the build's

board fence's line: the engraving draws the boards' top and foot almost level from x 670 to 990 px (top y 597-600, foot 652-658). On T-2437's re-solved camera a fence on the north lot line, running back from the street, cannot draw so: its foot rises as it recedes (y 655 px at the lot's corner, x 786; 643 at x 864; 633 at x 936; 625 at x 988), as the build's does. A fence on the STREET line running on north past the lot's corner draws exactly the drawn boards: top y 597.7 at x 864, 598.1 at 943, 598.6 at 1026; foot y 656.6, 658.5, 660.5. So the boards past x 786 px are the next lot's (1616's) street fence, read by T-2450 through this camera, and 1620's north lot-line fence stands behind them, its top 3-9 px over theirs and its foot hidden: this picture does not show that foot. The boards on 1620's own street line, x 670-786 px, are built and land on the drawn ones

walls' tone: the engraving draws the front light and the north wall and the pavilion's north half dark, its light from the south-east; the house's colour (the Inter Ocean's 'olive green' of 1887) and its walling are not shown in a monochrome print
the south side wall and the rear: the engraving sees neither
